smell_validity.evidence: Three role-specific traits — a top-level marker, a subcommand-grouping contract, and a single-subcommand contract — are collapsed into one CommandSpec forcing every command type to provide COMMAND, COMMANDS, and dynamic_commands(). Top-level structs synthesize unused identity entries; generic entry points depend on metadata they never read. The unwanted-obligation design mistake is clear and coherent, with no competing problems.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Adding any command type now requires providing all three capability members even when one suffices, and generic parsers transitively depend on the whole metadata surface. Removing the smell restores role-specific obligations so future additions and consumer edits are safer and shorter, though the derive auto-synthesizes the never-read placeholders, capping the practical safety gain.

development_plausibility.evidence: The change models a genuine consolidation refactor: merging adjacent role traits that all describe CommandInfo into one unified interface during API cleanup. Terminology, placement, and the derive's per-kind synthesized members grow naturally from argh's existing command-tree design; the over-consolidation reads as a believable compromise, not task-shaped filler.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: The prompt accurately names the problem (every role forced through one interface), lists the affected scope across both crates, and gives clear requirements plus a sharp preservation boundary (parsing, help, errors, dynamic subcommands, dispatch, boxed fields, signatures, tests). It rules out partial cleanups by insisting every instance across roles, codegen, and rendering be addressed, while leaving implementation open.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Distinct purposes require different decisions: redesigning the trait surface, emitting per-role derive impls (top-level drops metadata, subcommand keeps COMMAND, grouping keeps COMMANDS plus dynamic), re-pointing each consumer to the right capability trait, and re-bounding generic entry points to a parsing-only marker.

localization_burden.evidence: The prompt names the interface in the argh crate and points to derive codegen, help rendering, the missing-subcommand message, and dispatch code. A grep for CommandSpec finds all usages, but classifying each site by role and capability (COMMAND vs COMMANDS vs dynamic) requires tracing the trait through impls and consumers across several steps.

repair_coordination.evidence: Splitting the trait requires every impl and every consumer to preserve one shared rule: the role trait a type implements must match the role trait each consumer reads. Re-pointing consumers while leaving the derive's unified impl breaks compilation; the Box composition and grouping enum's forwarded members must coordinate with which capability consumers actually read.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: One uniform replacement (CommandSpec's COMMANDS and dynamic_commands reads to SubCommands) fixes the four collection-reading consumer sites, but the trait definition, per-role derive codegen, Box forwarding impl, generic bound reversion, and COMMAND dispatch reads each need separate, capability-specific decisions. A single rule covers well under 40% of locations.

behavioral_risk.evidence: Most wrong repairs fail Rust's type system immediately (a consumer reading a role trait the type lacks won't compile). The plausible behavioral wrong path — mis-editing the Box COMMANDS composition to an empty list, silently breaking boxed subcommand dispatch — is exercised by ordinary subcommand parsing that the preservation requirements keep stable.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
